title: Introduce connection-shelter orchestrator and deferred-circuit-unwind hotpatch
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Hotpatch: add connection-shelter orchestrator to smooth circuit transitions and reduce SLO violations during regional failover; automatic deferred unwind and telemetry anchor. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Context: During a recent regional failover incident (SUP-4827) we observed abrupt circuit flips causing a spike in 95th/99th latency and a short SLO breach for some tenant classes. This PR implements a lightweight runtime 'connection-shelter' and a deferred-circuit-unwind policy that: 1) preserves in-flight requests in a bounded shelter while circuit state transitions are computed; 2) defers circuit reopen/unwind for a short, telemetry-anchored window to avoid oscillation; 3) exposes per-tenant shelter metrics for SLO accounting. Motivation: provide a pragmatic, low-risk hotpatch that reduces tail spikes and gives the autoscaler and failover path time to stabilize before routes are forcibly reset. Checklist: - [x] implement shelter allocator and bounded queue with per-tenant caps - [x] wire deferred-unwind decision path into circuit manager with a small hysteresis window - [x] add telemetry (shelter_depth, shelter_drain_time, deferred_unwind_count) - [x] unit tests for boundary conditions and race windows - [x] integration test in perf-canary that simulates regional egress flaps Changes (high level): - runtime/circuit/connection_shelter.go: new in-memory shelter with eviction policy and drain hook - runtime/circuit/manager.go: integrate deferred-unwind policy, add decision hooks and metrics - infra/telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: register new metrics and dashboards notes - perf-canary/scenarios/shelter_drain.yaml: new canary scenario that replays regional disconnects - docs/operational/connection-shelter.md: short runbook and roll-back instructions Commits (summary): - Add connection shelter allocator and per-tenant caps - Integrate shelter with circuit manager and add deferred-unwind window - Add metrics, dashboards, and canary scenario - Tests: unit+integration for race and boundary cases - Fix: reduce default shelter time-to-drain from 5s -> 2s after perf tests Review summary: - Jared Kim (SRE) requested stronger telemetry and an opt-out flag per-tenant; author added tenant opt-out in manager config and extra metrics (shelter_evictions_total) - Lucia Moreno requested that the shelter not exceed connection memory budget; added dynamic cap based on process memory headroom and a safe-guard to force immediate unwind if memory pressure is critical - Evan Brooks asked for a clearer rollback path and a shorter default drain; author reduced default and added a feature-flag gating the behavior for immediate rollback if we see regressions Discussion thread ( high level): - Jared: "Can we get a histogram of shelter_drain_time by tenant tier?" - Aisha: "Added histogram and dashboard; also added a Linear card for SRE to monitor the 95th during canary." - Lucia: "Under memory pressure, we should prefer immediate unwind over OOM risk." - Aisha: "Added memory-pressure fast-path; documented in runbook." CI and validation: - Initial CI run had a flaky integration failure in perf-canary (timeout on scenario orchestration). Re-ran the canary job with extended timeout; all checks passed. - perf-canary run (staging) shows 30-40% reduction in transient 99th latency spikes for affected route samples. Canary verdict: passed with no regressions in throughput. Rollout plan: - Rollout to Dedicated in a canary tranche (2 pools) for 2 hours, monitor shelter_* metrics and 99th latency - If canary is healthy, lift gate to 25% of traffic for 6 hours, then full rollout. Hotpatch notes: this is intended as a low-risk runtime change with a feature flag (runtime.feature.connection_shelter) enabled by default for SRE and disabled per tenant unless opted-in. Merge: squash and merge after approvals. This PR addresses SUP-4827 and should reduce oscillatory reopen events observed during the incident.
